description: Reported HCL array & string hashing problems: exact pair-sum counting with duplicates and first unique character index.

problems.title: Count Pairs with Given Sum
problems.statement: Given an integer array A of size N and a target integer K, count the total number of index pairs (i, j) with 0 <= i < j < N such that A[i] + A[j] == K. Duplicates are allowed and each distinct index pair counts separately.
problems.inputFormat:
Line 1: Two integers N and K.
Line 2: N space-separated integers A[0..N-1].
problems.outputFormat: A single integer representing the count of pairs.

solutions.python:
import sys
from collections import defaultdict

data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n, k = data[0], data[1]
freq = defaultdict(int)
count = 0
for x in data[2:2+n]:
    count += freq[k - x]
    freq[x] += 1
print(count)

problems.timeComplexity: O(N) average time via single-pass hash map lookup.
edgeCases: All identical elements equal to K/2 ('1 1 1 1', K=2 => 6 pairs)
Pair count up to N*(N-1)/2 overflows 32-bit int when N=10^5 -> use `long`
